prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” interior painting company in St. Louis — the right choice depends on your budget, the size and complexity of the job, your timeline, and whether you want extras (color consulting, drywall repair, specialty finishes, low-VOC paint, etc.). Instead of naming one firm, here’s a practical way to find the best painter for your project and a short checklist you can use to compare candidates.

How to find the best interior painter for you
1. Search local reviews and referrals
 - Check Google Maps, Yelp, Angi/HomeAdvisor, BBB, Nextdoor, and local Facebook groups for recent reviews and photos.  
 - Ask neighbors or real estate agents for referrals and to see completed work in person.

2. Narrow to 3 candidates
 - Pick three painters with strong recent reviews, good photos of similar work, and valid insurance.

3. Get written estimates
 - Ask for itemized, written bids that show prep, number of coats, paint brand + sheen, labor and materials, cleanup, and start/finish dates.

4. Verify credentials
 - Confirm they carry general liability and workers’ comp insurance.  
 - Ask for local references (phone numbers) and a portfolio of recent projects like yours.  
 - If your house was built before 1978, ask about lead-safe practices and certification (EPA RRP).

5. Compare apples-to-apples
 - Make sure bids specify the same prep work (sanding, patching, priming), paint quality, number of coats, and warranties.

6. Contract and payment
 - Get a written contract with schedule, payment terms (typical: small deposit, balance on completion), cleanup and touch-up policy, and warranty details.  
 - Avoid large upfront payments.

Questions to ask every painter
 - How long have you been in business in the St. Louis area?  
 - Are you licensed/insured? Can I see proof?  
 - Can you provide 3 recent references with similar interior jobs?  
 - What brand and grade of paint will you use? How many coats?  
 - What prep work is included (patching, priming, sanding, caulking)?  
 - Do you use subcontractors or your own crew?  
 - What is the start date and estimated completion date?  
 - Do you offer color consultation? Any warranty or touch-up policy?  
 - How do you handle unexpected issues/cost changes?  
 - Do you follow EPA RRP rules if lead paint might be present?

Red flags
 - No insurance or unwillingness to show proof.  
 - Very low bid that’s far below others (may cut corners).  
 - Vague or verbal-only estimates and contracts.  
 - Poor or no references, many recent negative reviews that mention the same issue.

If you want, I can:
 - Provide a short phone/email script you can use to request bids.  
 - Create a one-page comparison checklist so you can compare three estimates side-by-side.  
 - Narrow options if you tell me your ZIP code, budget, size of the job (rooms/sq ft), and any special requirements (lead-safe, low-VOC, color consult).

Which of those would be most useful right now?
